Other lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) need their own UN Regulations (not supplied) under 5.6; single-mark option 5.6.1 and 5.6.2 identification symbols depend on approval architecture.
Whether the LED modules are replaceable, non-replaceable or 'light source modules' under R7 is unknown. This decides applicability of 3.2, 3.4, 3.6 and 2.2.2, so those requirements are conditional.
Applicability of 3.5 (secondary design voltage) and of variable intensity provisions (2.2.3, 2.2.4) cannot be determined; the electronics and intensity control are unspecified.

Approval mark composition (4.2, 4.1.5), module rated-voltage marking (3.6.3) and grouped-lamp rules (4.1.2) are on a context page; they are referenced but not extracted here.
Paragraph 1.2 limits ESA coverage by paragraph 3.2.1, which is not in the supplied pages. Applicability to the lamp is unresolved.

Section 2.12 lists stop and rear position lamps as immunity related functions, but immunity requirements, test levels and acceptance criteria are in later sections not supplied. No engineering requirement can be derived.
The spec leaves the approval route (component, STU or vehicle-level) and any electronic drivers or control electronics unstated. R10 applicability depends on these.

Annex 2 (marking models, AR symbol arrangement), Annex 1 and paragraph 5.5 are referenced but not supplied.

Product facts unknown: light source replaceability, whether LED modules are light source modules, and grouping or shared lens arrangement; applicability of R2, R4 to R8 and R12 to R15 is conditional on these.
